assertion.name: Inability to walk
assertion.description: Gross motor function is severely limited. Among the individuals graded on the Gross Motor Function Classification System, roughly six in ten were level V with a further quarter at level IV, so about 86% of those graded are non-ambulatory and require full physical assistance. Motor impairment of some degree was present in almost all individuals with available data.
assertion.notes: Denominator, stated explicitly because it is not the pooled cohort. The GMFCS percentages do not run over the 51 pooled individuals; they resolve arithmetically to n=22, since 59.09% is 13/22, 27.27% is 6/22, 9.09% is 2/22 and 4.55% is 1/22, which sum to 22 individuals and to 100%. The deep research artifact records the GMFCS subgroup as n=22 explicitly, and the same paper reports motor impairment over a different subgroup again (97.83%, i.e. 45/46), so denominators vary from section to section. The cached paper's own prose conflicts with its own arithmetic. It reads "All individuals were assessed using the Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS)", which taken literally would put the denominator at 51. The arithmetic is preferred here over the prose. The band is chosen on the n=22 reading: 19 of the 22 individuals actually graded (86.36%) were at GMFCS level IV or V, both of which denote non-ambulatory status requiring physical assistance, and 86.36% is above 80% and so maps to VERY_FREQUENT. On the alternative reading, in which the same 19 individuals are taken over the full pooled cohort, 19/51 is 37% and the band would be FREQUENT. The n=22 reading is used because individuals who were not graded are unknown rather than known to be ambulatory, which is the usual convention for frequency denominators; a reader who instead treats the paper's "All individuals" wording as authoritative should read this band as FREQUENT. Note that the entry deliberately omits three other frequency bands (for example infantile epileptic spasms syndrome, 16/24 with detailed epilepsy data but 16/51 of the cohort) where the denominator is unknown, is very small, or is conditioned in a way that leaves no principled choice between readings. Here the band is retained rather than dropped because the subgroup denominator is recoverable exactly from the published percentages and both readings are recorded. The 9.09% at level III walk with a handheld mobility device and the 4.55% at level II are ambulatory with limitations.

assertion.name: Decreased Circulating ACTH
assertion.description: Plasma ACTH is low or suppressed, because autonomous adrenal cortisol production shuts down pituitary corticotrophs. This is the feature that makes the syndrome ACTH-INDEPENDENT and separates it from Cushing disease, so it is definitional for the entity rather than incidental.
assertion.notes:
Evidenced at the level of PBMAH rather than of KDM1A-related PBMAH specifically. None of the KDM1A cohort papers reports ACTH values, so the citations below are a PBMAH case report and a PBMAH review. The inference to KDM1A carriers is safe - ACTH-independence is definitional for the parent entity and the KDM1A form is a subset of it - but it is an inference, and the evidence grading says so.
One nuance the entry does not smooth over: a 2026 review notes intra-adrenal ACTH production by steroidogenic cells in PBMAH, so "ACTH-independent" refers to independence from PITUITARY ACTH, not to the absence of ACTH signalling altogether.

selected_evidence.snippet: Aberrant hormone receptor expression and intra-adrenal adrenocorticotropin production by steroidogenic cells may also contribute to cortisol dysregulation in many patients.

selected_evidence.snippet: Nephrotic syndrome and renal insufficiency were noted in 63.1% and 75% of patients, respectively.

assertion.name: Macroglossia
assertion.description: Macroglossia can occur; its relative rarity in AA does not make it an exclusionary finding.

selected_evidence.snippet: Other frequently encountered presenting symptoms include weight loss, abdominal pain, malabsorption, macroglossia, gastroesophageal reflux, esophageal dysmotility, gastric polyps, and episodes of upper and lower gastrointestinal bleeding

assertion.name: Weight Loss
assertion.description: Weight loss is reported among gastrointestinal presentations; the relative contributions of malabsorption and systemic illness vary.

selected_evidence.snippet: Other frequently encountered presenting symptoms include weight loss, abdominal pain, malabsorption, macroglossia, gastroesophageal reflux, esophageal dysmotility, gastric polyps, and episodes of upper and lower gastrointestinal bleeding

assertion.name: Hepatomegaly
assertion.description: Hepatomegaly can develop with hepatic deposition. Imaging evidence of deposition does not necessarily imply functional liver disease.

selected_evidence.snippet: Hepato- and splenomegaly commonly manifests during disease progression, whereas splenic rupture is exceptionally rare

assertion.name: Malabsorption
assertion.description: Amyloid infiltration of the bowel wall impairs absorption, contributing with chronic diarrhoea to the weight loss seen in advanced disease.

selected_evidence.snippet: Other frequently encountered presenting symptoms include weight loss, abdominal pain, malabsorption, macroglossia, gastroesophageal reflux, esophageal dysmotility, gastric polyps, and episodes of upper and lower gastrointestinal bleeding

assertion.name: Peripheral Edema
assertion.description: Edema can accompany nephrotic protein loss and hypervolemia.

selected_evidence.snippet: Classification as nephrotic required a 24-hour urinary excretion of more than 3 g of protein, a serum albumin concentration of less than 3.4 g per deciliter, and either the presence of peripheral edema or the use of diuretics to treat peripheral edema.

assertion.name: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase
assertion.description: The review reports elevated alkaline phosphatase in approximately 5% of patients. This nonspecific finding does not by itself establish hepatic amyloid injury.

selected_evidence.snippet: Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels are noted in 5% of patients

assertion.name: Proteinuria
assertion.description: Proteinuria is a major renal presentation, especially with glomerular deposition. The review groups proteinuria with declining kidney function in its >90% estimate, so that percentage is not assigned to proteinuria alone.

selected_evidence.snippet: The clinical presentation of glomerular and vascular forms was distinct with a clear predominance of proteinuria in glomerular form.

assertion.name: Hypoalbuminemia
assertion.description: Reduced serum albumin resulting from urinary protein loss; a component of the nephrotic syndrome and a marker of its severity.

selected_evidence.snippet: Classification as nephrotic required a 24-hour urinary excretion of more than 3 g of protein, a serum albumin concentration of less than 3.4 g per deciliter, and either the presence of peripheral edema or the use of diuretics to treat peripheral edema.

assertion.name: Splenomegaly
assertion.description: Splenomegaly can occur during progression. Splenic deposits can be imaged even when clinically silent; rupture is exceptionally rare.

selected_evidence.snippet: Hepato- and splenomegaly commonly manifests during disease progression, whereas splenic rupture is exceptionally rare

assertion.name: Hypocalcemia
assertion.description: Parathyroid dysfunction in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome ranges from severe neonatal hypocalcemia to subclinical hypoparathyroidism. No frequency band is assigned here because the retained sources do not provide a directly applicable population estimate.

selected_evidence.snippet: calcium supplementation and referral to an endocrinologist and nephrologist because of increased risk of renal calculi if long-term supplementation is required

assertion.name: Velopharyngeal insufficiency
assertion.description: Failure of the velopharyngeal port to close during speech is the "velo" component of the historical velocardiofacial (Shprintzen) presentation. GeneReviews lists velopharyngeal incompetence alongside - rather than as a consequence of - submucous and overt cleft palate, so it is curated separately from the palatal structural anomalies above. Note that the literature treats velopharyngeal dysfunction in this syndrome as broader than velopharyngeal insufficiency alone; this phenotype is bound to the insufficiency term, and the additional contributors are modelled in the upstream mechanism node.

selected_evidence.snippet: While not all people with 22q have a palatal abnormality, up to 80% of people with 22q present with VPI.

assertion.name: Learning difficulties
assertion.description: Learning difficulties and developmental differences are common clinical concerns, but they should not be equated automatically with intellectual disability.

selected_evidence.snippet: learning difficulties

assertion.name: Hypernasal speech
assertion.description: Hypernasal resonance is the audible speech consequence of the incompetent velopharyngeal port and is the feature that most often brings affected children to speech surgery. Its persistence after palatoplasty in this syndrome is attributed to pharyngeal anatomy and muscle tone rather than to a residual palatal cleft.

selected_evidence.snippet: Resonance and speech sound disorders may also present and include hypernasality and compensatory misarticulation errors that require speech therapy.

assertion.name: Cellular immunodeficiency
assertion.description: T-cell lymphopenia varies from mild laboratory reduction to clinically important immune dysfunction; immune severity cannot be inferred from external syndromic features alone.

selected_evidence.snippet: An estimated 67–80% of individuals affected with 22q11.2del have some degree of T cell lymphopenia (TCL).

assertion.name: Velopharyngeal insufficiency
assertion.description: Failure of the velopharyngeal port to close during speech is the "velo" component of the historical velocardiofacial (Shprintzen) presentation. GeneReviews lists velopharyngeal incompetence alongside - rather than as a consequence of - submucous and overt cleft palate, so it is curated separately from the palatal structural anomalies above. Note that the literature treats velopharyngeal dysfunction in this syndrome as broader than velopharyngeal insufficiency alone; this phenotype is bound to the insufficiency term, and the additional contributors are modelled in the upstream mechanism node.

selected_evidence.snippet: 22q11.2DS presents a uniquely high burden of ENT disease across the lifespan, including chronic otitis media, elevated cholesteatoma risk, persistent velopharyngeal dysfunction, multilevel airway anomalies, sleep-disordered breathing, dysphagia, and perioperative vulnerability due to vascular, immunologic, and hematologic anomalies.

assertion.name: Delayed speech and language development
assertion.description: Language impairment is broad rather than confined to a single domain, and it is not fully explained by speech intelligibility - children with intelligible speech still score below average, so this is curated separately from the palatal and resonance phenotypes above and from general learning difficulties.

selected_evidence.snippet: Additionally, most people (95%) with 22q present with a speech-language disorder.

assertion.name: Genitourinary anomaly
assertion.description: Structural genitourinary anomalies are part of the variable multisystem phenotype and warrant directed evaluation.

selected_evidence.snippet: Laryngotracheoesophageal, gastrointestinal, ophthalmologic, central nervous system, skeletal, and genitourinary anomalies also occur.

assertion.name: Schizophrenia
assertion.description: Meta-analysis estimated schizophrenia in 9.7% of individuals with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, with higher psychotic-disorder prevalence in adult samples.

selected_evidence.snippet: The pooled prevalence of psychotic disorders was 11.50% (95%CI:9.40-14.00%), largely schizophrenia (9.70%, 95%CI:6.50-14.20).

selected_evidence.snippet: Patients with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11DelS) often present with velopharyngeal dysfunction (VPD). VPD in patients with 22q11DelS is multifactorial beyond velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) alone, and differences in surgical outcomes are poorly understood.

assertion.name: Obesity
assertion.notes: Frequency is age-dependent: the review estimates that 75% are obese by adulthood. Childhood BMI trajectories do not imply that all young children are obese.

selected_evidence.snippet: Obesity is a feature of this disorder and generally emerges in childhood; BMI in individuals with the 16p11.2 recurrent deletion is significantly higher than in the general population by age five years.

assertion.name: Deeply Set Eyes
assertion.notes: Reported in the ocular case-literature review. Its percentages use 43 cases selected for documented eye findings and are not population frequencies for deletion carriers.

selected_evidence.snippet: From a systematic review of prior reported cases, the most common eye and ocular adnexa findings observed were downslanting palpebral fissures, deep-set eyes, ptosis, and hypertelorism.

selected_evidence.snippet: Seizures are observed in approximately 25% of individuals with the recurrent deletion.

assertion.name: Chiari Type I Malformation
assertion.notes: The 9% estimate comes from a clinical MRI cohort, not unselected carriers.

selected_evidence.snippet: Indeed, we found that deletion carriers had a thicker corpus callosum compared to controls and that 30% of the deletion carriers had cerebellar tonsillar ectopia and 9% had radiologically defined Chiari I malformations [31].
Sacral dimples were noted in 34%, but without an associated tethered cord when assess by imaging.
